title: Lift a giant pumpkin with a plank
_map: Levers and gears (stretch, usually Y5). Big idea: simple machines make jobs easier. Creative: lift a heavy pumpkin with a lever; connect gears to make the mill turn fast or slow.
_story: The giant pumpkin is too heavy for Steve to lift. A plank and a log make a lever. Then the mill turns too slowly, and gears fix it. Like Create mod machines, but real.
_stepChain: heavy things are hard to lift → a plank on a log is a lever → the log is the pivot → pivot close to the pumpkin: easy → gears: teeth push each other round → a small gear turns a big gear slowly, a big gear turns a small gear fast → machines make jobs easier

talk.ask: Where should the pivot go to lift the pumpkin most easily?
talk.goodAnswer: close to the pumpkin; then you push down on the long end.

talk.ask: If a small gear turns a big gear, does the big gear turn faster or slower?
talk.goodAnswer: slower: the small gear has to go round more times to turn the big one once.

handsOn: Make a seesaw from a ruler and a pencil. Put a toy on one end and press the other. Move the pencil closer to the toy: is it easier? Then look for gears in a bike.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Hnnnngh! My giant pumpkin is too heavy to lift onto the cart! I tried and tried! Ismaeel, have you got an idea?

Here's a trick! Put a long plank over a log, with the pumpkin on one end. Push down on the other end, and… up goes the pumpkin! Whoa! A plank that tips on a point like that is called a lever. The point it tips on is called the pivot.
Where should the log go, to make lifting easiest?

question.prompt: Pivot close to the pumpkin, or close to Steve?
question.reveal: Close to the pumpkin! Then Steve pushes on the long end, and even a little push lifts the heavy pumpkin! Easy as anything!

narration.text: Now the windmill! A wheel with teeth round the edge is called a gear. When two gears touch, their teeth push each other round. Click, click, click! Here, a little gear with 8 teeth turns a big gear with 16 teeth.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: The big gear has twice as many teeth. So it must turn twice as fast!

question.prompt: Does the big gear turn faster, or slower, than the little one?
question.onRight: Yes! The little gear goes round twice, for every once the big gear turns!

0.hint: The little gear has 8 teeth. How many times must it turn, to push all 16 teeth of the big one past?
0.say: The little gear's 8 teeth have to go round twice, to push all 16 teeth of the big gear round once! So the big gear turns more slowly.

question.reveal: Big gear: slower, but stronger. Little gear: faster!

rule.text: Levers and gears make jobs easier.
rule.ask: Where should a lever's pivot go, to lift something heavy? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: A lever lifts heavy things more easily when the pivot is close to the load. Gears change speed: a small gear turns a big gear slowly.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! On a bike, which gear makes going up a hill easiest?
choices: A big gear at the back
A small gear at the back
bonus.reveal: A big gear at the back! Your legs go round more times, but each push is easier.
